speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help me pinpoint the cause, how long have you been feeling these symptoms?

Did this onset happen suddenly, like in a blink of an eye, or did it develop gradually over days or weeks?

Have you noticed any other symptoms such as numbness in your leg, slurred speech, facial drooping, or severe headache?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome secondary to cervical rib or hypertrophied scalene muscles, though peripheral neuropathy from diabetes and anabolic steroid myopathy remain important differential considerations. The patient's weight loss and weakness warrant imaging of the cervical spine and brachial plexus to rule out structural compression or neoplasm.

REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI_with_brachial_plexus_fat_saturation, Chest_X-Ray_ap_view.

REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Studies_and_Electromyography.
